evidence.locator: JSON product, 5,441 planets, each with its star's four habitable zone distances in au (hz_r0_au to hz_r3_au: optimistic inner, conservative inner, conservative outer, optimistic outer; the same four as the CSV table's OHZIN, CHZIN, CHZOUT, OHZOUT) and the stellar temperature and luminosity they were calculated from. The seven rows of TRAPPIST-1 agree: 0.0194, 0.0246, 0.0499 and 0.0527 au, from 2,566 K and 0.000553 solar luminosities.

The five rows of 55 Cnc do not agree: planet e's row gives 0.5870, 0.7435, 1.3367 and 1.4098 au from 5,172 K, 0.943 solar radii and 0.571 solar luminosities (Bourrier et al. 2018's star); the rows of b, c, d and f give 0.6153, 0.7794, 1.3999 and 1.4765 au from 5,198 K, 0.98 solar radii and 0.629 solar luminosities.
The two rows of Proxima Cen agree: 0.0320, 0.0405, 0.0810 and 0.0854 au, from 2,900 K and 0.00151 solar luminosities.

Frequently asked questions: the boundaries follow Kopparapu et al. (2013, 2014); the conservative model uses the runaway greenhouse and maximum greenhouse limits, the optimistic model the recent Venus and early Mars limits; stellar and planetary parameters are taken from the NASA Exoplanet Archive.
The 2 rows of LHS 1140 agree: 0.0506, 0.0641, 0.1270 and 0.1340 au, from 3096 K and 0.0038 solar luminosities.
The 2 rows of K2-18 agree: 0.1204, 0.1526, 0.2969 and 0.3132 au, from 3457 K and 0.02166 solar luminosities.
The 5 rows of Kepler-186 disagree; Kepler-186 f's row: 0.1910, 0.2420, 0.4641 and 0.4895 au, from 3755 K and 0.05495 solar luminosities.
The 1 row of Kepler-452 agree: 0.8283, 1.0492, 1.8512 and 1.9526 au, from 5757 K and 1.215 solar luminosities.

statements.text: This research has made use of the Habitable Zone Gallery at hzgallery.org. Cite Kane & Gelino (2012), PASP 124, 323.
